Run network proximity, drug-pair analysis, RevERT, and virtual screening from R.
All steps run on CPU.

## 1. Install once

Use R 4.5 and RStudio, or R with Pandoc. Linux also needs R build tools
(`r-base-dev` on Ubuntu). Open this Rmd in RStudio and use `tutorial/`
as your working directory.

Run once to install the R packages and Python CPU dependencies. This needs
internet access.

```{r install, eval=FALSE}
source("../install.R", chdir = TRUE)
```

After installation, run the remaining chunks or click **Knit**. Knitting skips
installation and works offline. From `tutorial/`, you can also run:

```{r render-instructions, eval=FALSE}
rmarkdown::render("DIMER_workflow.Rmd")
```

## 2. Load the example data

The network and expression data are simulated: four drugs (`DrugA`–`DrugD`),
30 targets (`TargetA`–`TargetZ`, `TargetAA`–`TargetAD`), and a six-gene disease
module. The screening step uses real compound structures and an LRRK2 sequence.

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(error = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(data.table)
dir.create("output", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

source("../core/NetworkProximity/load_reference.R")
source("../core/NetworkProximity/static_proximity.R")
source("../core/NetworkProximity/set_distance.R")
source("../core/NetworkProximity/combination.R")
source("../core/FunctionalDirection/direction_score.R")
```

```{r inputs}
ppi = load_ppi("input/ppi_edges.csv")
module_genes = readLines("input/disease_genes.txt")
dti = load_dti(
  "input/drug_targets.csv",
  drug_col = "drug", name_col = "drug_name",
  type_col = "drug_type", gene_col = "target_gene"
)$dti
blacklist = load_blacklist("input/drug_pair_blacklist.csv")
knitr::kable(dti[, .(drug, target_gene)])
```

## 3. Rank drugs by network proximity

A negative `static_z` means targets are closer to the disease module than
expected from degree-matched random gene sets. We use 100 permutations here;
increase this for your analysis.

```{r proximity}
proximity = run_static_proximity(
  ppi, module_genes, dti, n_perm = 100, seed = 1
)
fwrite(proximity, "output/static_proximity.csv")
knitr::kable(
  proximity[, .(drug, observed_distance, static_z, static_p)],
  digits = 3
)
```

## 4. Evaluate drug pairs

Calculate target-set separation and network classes. The example blacklist
excludes `DrugA`–`DrugD`, leaving five pairs. Class P2 means both drugs are
proximal to the module and their target sets are separated.

```{r combinations}
combination = run_drug_combination(
  module_genes, proximity$drug, ppi, dti,
  blacklist = blacklist, drug_scores = proximity
)
fwrite(combination$pairs, "output/drug_pairs.csv")
fwrite(combination$removed_by_blacklist, "output/blacklisted_pairs.csv")
knitr::kable(
  combination$pairs[, .(drug_a, drug_b, network_class, s_ab)], digits = 3
)
```

## 5. Evaluate transcriptional reversal with RevERT

Disease signs of +1/−1 indicate increased/decreased expression versus control.
Drug effects use the same convention for treatment versus control.
A positive RevERT score indicates reversal of the disease signature.

```{r direction}
signature = fread("input/disease_signature.csv")
perturbations = fread("input/drug_perturbations.csv")
direction = rbindlist(lapply(proximity$drug, function(id) {
  effect = setNames(perturbations[[id]], perturbations$gene)
  cbind(
    data.frame(drug = id),
    direction_score(signature, effect, drug_term = "sign")
  )
}))
setnames(direction, "score", "revert_score")
direction$revert_fdr = p.adjust(direction$p, method = "BH")
fwrite(direction, "output/revert_scores.csv")
knitr::kable(direction[, .(drug, revert_score, n_overlap, revert_fdr)], digits = 3)
```

Join reversal and proximity scores:

```{r prioritize}
prioritization = merge(
  proximity,
  direction[, .(drug, revert_score, n_overlap, revert_fdr)],
  by = "drug"
)
setorder(prioritization, static_z)
fwrite(prioritization, "output/drug_prioritization.csv")
knitr::kable(
  prioritization[, .(drug, static_z, revert_score)], digits = 3
)
```

## 6. Run virtual screening on CPU from R

Screen eight compounds against LRRK2 using pretrained VecNet weights and
bundled reference binders. `device = "cpu"` runs without a GPU;
`finetune = FALSE` uses the pretrained model directly.

```{r screening-setup}
source("../core/VirtualScreening/R/vecnet_component.R")
vecnet_init()
reticulate::import("torch")$set_num_threads(1L)

targets = vecnet_read_fasta("input/targets.fasta")
compounds = read.csv("input/compounds.csv")
library_smiles = setNames(compounds$smiles, compounds$compound_id)
references = vecnet_reference_binders(names(targets))
```

```{r screen}
screening = run_virtual_screening(
  targets = targets,
  library = library_smiles,
  device = "cpu",
  finetune = FALSE,
  known_binders = references$known_binders,
  reference_ligand = references$reference_ligand,
  similarity_band = "auto"
)
screening_report = attr(screening, "report")
ranking = as.data.table(screening)
setorder(ranking, target, -combined)
ranking$rank = ave(seq_len(nrow(ranking)), ranking$target, FUN = seq_along)
setcolorder(ranking, c("rank", "compound_id", "smiles", "target"))
fwrite(ranking, "output/virtual_screening.csv")
knitr::kable(
  ranking[, .(rank, compound_id, target, score, similarity, combined)],
  digits = 4
)
```

Higher `combined` scores rank first. Scores do not estimate binding affinity
or establish drug efficacy.

```{r checks, include=FALSE}
stopifnot(
  nrow(proximity) == 4L,
  all(is.finite(proximity$static_z)),
  all(proximity$static_p > 0 & proximity$static_p <= 1),
  nrow(combination$pairs) == 5L,
  nrow(combination$removed_by_blacklist) == 1L,
  direction[drug == "DrugA", revert_score] == 1,
  direction[drug == "DrugC", revert_score] == -1,
  nrow(ranking) == 8L,
  all(is.finite(as.matrix(ranking[, .(score, similarity, combined)])))
)
```

```{r runtime-info, include=FALSE}
writeLines(
  c("n_perm = 100; seed = 1; drug_term = sign", capture.output(sessionInfo())),
  "output/R_session_info.txt"
)
screening_report$python = reticulate::import("sys")$version
metadata = reticulate::import("importlib.metadata")
packages = c("torch", "numpy", "pandas", "scipy", "rdkit", "gensim", "scikit-learn")
screening_report$packages = as.list(setNames(
  vapply(packages, function(p) metadata$version(p), character(1)), packages
))
screening_report$similarity_band = unique(ranking[, .(target, similarity_band)])
jsonlite::write_json(
  screening_report, "output/virtual_screening_report.json",
  pretty = TRUE, auto_unbox = TRUE, null = "null"
)
```

Results and software versions are saved in `output/`.
Expect four drug results, five drug pairs, and eight screened compounds.
Rerunning replaces these files.

## 7. Use your own data

Replace the files in `input/` and remove or adapt the `checks` chunk.
Use matching gene and drug IDs across files.

| Input | Format |
|---|---|
| `disease_genes.txt` | One gene ID per line |
| `ppi_edges.csv` | `gene_a,gene_b`, one undirected interaction per row |
| `drug_targets.csv` | `drug,drug_name,drug_type,target_gene`; repeat a drug for multiple targets |
| `drug_pair_blacklist.csv` | `drug_a,drug_b`; IDs must match the drug-target table |
| `disease_signature.csv` | `gene,sign,weight`; disease-versus-control signs of +1 or −1 |
| `drug_perturbations.csv` | `gene` followed by one numeric drug-effect column per drug ID |
| `targets.fasta` | Protein sequences; FASTA header IDs identify targets |
| `compounds.csv` | `compound_id,smiles` |

For other screening targets, supply matching binders or omit `known_binders`,
`reference_ligand`, and `similarity_band` and rank by `score`.
